h1: The 7 Best Power Strips for Desks of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Power Strips for Desks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven surge-protected power strips for desks in 2026, compared on joules, outlet spacing, USB ports and cord length.
summary: The Amazon Basics 12-outlet strip is the best power strip for a desk, with the highest rating here at 4000 joules and an 8 ft cord for under $25. The ALESTOR is the pick if you want 4 USB ports at 2700 joules, and the Nuetsa solves tight wall clearance with a flat plug.
intro: A desk power strip has two jobs, and most buyers check only one. Outlet count gets the attention, but the joule rating decides how much surge energy the strip can absorb before its protection parts wear out. A 12-outlet strip with a tiny joule number is a power splitter wearing a safety label.

Every strip here sits in the under $25 bucket, so price is not the separator. We reviewed the specs and ranked on joules, outlet layout, USB ports, cord length and safety listing, leaving out review counts. Joules run from 790 to 4000 across the group, a fivefold spread, and that gap matters most for a desk loaded with a computer, monitors and chargers, where a single bad storm can hit everything at once.

products.name: Amazon Basics 12-Outlet Surge Protector Power Strip, 4000 Joules, 8ft Extension Cord, Rectangle, for Home, Office, Gaming Room, Black
products.verdict: The highest joule rating here, with 12 outlets and an 8 ft cord.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics 12-outlet strip lists 4000 joules, 12 outlets and an 8 ft cord in a rectangle form factor, for under $25. Joules describe the total surge energy the protection components can absorb over their life, so a higher number means the strip protects for more events before it needs replacing.

It wins because 4000 joules is the most surge headroom in the guide, nearly double the Anker's 2100 and well above the 2700 joule picks. It also gives the longest cord at 8 ft, 2 ft more than the ALESTOR. The tradeoff is that the listing shows no USB ports, so phones need a separate charger.

Buy it for a gaming or work desk with a computer, monitors and a dock. The caveat is plug bulk: the rectangular plug can crowd a nearby wall outlet.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the most surge-protection headroom for a demanding full desk setup.

products.name: Power Strip, ALESTOR Surge Protector with 12 Outlets and 4 USB Ports, 6 Feet Extension Cord, 2700 Joules, ETL Listed, Black
products.verdict: 12 outlets and 4 USB ports at 2700 joules, ETL listed.
products.description:
The ALESTOR lists 12 outlets, 4 USB ports, 2700 joules, an ETL listing and a 6 ft cord, for under $25. ETL means an independent lab certified the strip to a safety standard, which not every cheap strip states. The USB ports free up outlets that a phone charger would otherwise take.

It takes second place because its 2700 joules trail the Amazon Basics' 4000, and its cord is 2 ft shorter. But it matches the top pick on outlet count and adds four USB ports, which the leader lacks. Against the Nuetsa at the same joules, it offers four extra outlets.

Buy it for a full desk with phones, tablets and a wide set of plugs. The caveat is that joule gap: if you run costly electronics, the extra headroom of the leader counts.
cons: Lower joules than the top pick
products.idealFor: Buyers who want maximum outlets with genuine surge protection for a full desk setup.

products.name: Surge Protector Power Strip - Nuetsa Flat Plug Extension Cord with 8 Outlets and 4 USB Ports, 6 Feet Power Cord, 2700 Joules, ETL Listed, Black
products.verdict: A flat plug lets a desk sit close to the wall.
products.description:
The Nuetsa has 8 outlets, 4 USB ports, a flat plug, a 6 ft cord, 2700 joules and an ETL listing, for under $25. A flat plug sits flush against the wall, so a desk or sofa can sit tight to the outlet without crushing the cord.

It ranks third because it has four fewer outlets than the ALESTOR for the same joules and the same USB count. What it adds is the plug shape, and that matters in rooms where the outlet sits behind furniture. A rectangle plug on the Amazon Basics sticks out several inches more.

Buy it when the outlet is tucked behind a desk. The caveat is outlet count: eight is enough for most desks, but if you need a dozen plugs, step up to the ALESTOR.
products.idealFor: Buyers whose desk sits close to a wall outlet needing flat-plug clearance.

products.name: Anker Power Strip with 2100J Surge Protector, Outlet Extender, 20W, 12 AC
products.verdict: 12 AC outlets at 2100 joules with a 20W output.
products.description:
The Anker strip lists 12 AC outlets, 2100 joules and a 20W output, for under $25. The Anker name is what many buyers pay for. A well-known maker usually means clearer support and a safer record than anonymous listings.

It ranks fourth because its 2100 joules sit below the 2700 and 4000 joule picks, and the listing does not state the cord length. The 20W output gives modest USB charging, but not enough to justify the lower surge rating over the ALESTOR, which has 4 ports and more joules at the same bracket.

Buy it if the brand matters and you have a typical desk. The caveat is surge capacity and the unlisted cord length, so check the feet before you plan the layout.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want an established-brand surge-protected strip for a full desk.
products.skipIf: Surge capacity is your top priority.

products.name: 6Ft Power Strip Surge Protector - Yintar Extension Cord with 6 AC Outlets and 3 USB Ports for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, 1680 Joules, ETL Listed, (Black)
products.verdict: A compact 6-outlet strip with 3 USB ports at 1680 joules.
products.description:
The Yintar lists 6 AC outlets, 3 USB ports, 1680 joules, an ETL listing and a 6 ft cord, in a compact design, for under $25. Six outlets and three USB ports cover a laptop, a monitor, a lamp and a phone, which is all many people run.

It ranks fifth because it offers half the outlets of the 12-outlet picks and lower joules than the ALESTOR or Nuetsa. Its compact body suits a dorm or small desk where a long strip would dangle. It also has more joules than the 790 joule Amazon Basics 6-outlet and adds USB.

Buy it for a standard desk or a dorm. The caveat is headroom: heavier setups will want more outlets and a higher joule number.
products.idealFor: Buyers with a standard desk setup who want a balance of outlets and USB ports.

products.name: Amazon Basics Surge Protector Power Strip, 6-Outlet, 790 Joules, Circuit Breaker, LED Indicator, 6ft Extension Cord, White
products.verdict: A basic 6-outlet strip with a circuit breaker and LED protection indicator.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics 6-outlet strip lists 6 outlets, 790 joules, a circuit breaker, an LED protection indicator and a 6 ft cord, for under $25. The LED matters more than it sounds. Surge components wear out silently, and an indicator tells you when protection has stopped.

It ranks sixth because 790 joules is the lowest rating here, a fraction of the 4000 joule Amazon Basics 12-outlet. But the indicator and breaker are real safety features, and several higher-rated strips do not list an indicator at all. It also lacks USB, unlike the Yintar.

Buy it for a light setup, such as a laptop and a lamp. The caveat is rating: heavy users with expensive gear should step up to a higher-joule strip.
products.idealFor: Budget-conscious buyers with a standard desk setup and modest outlet needs.

products.name: 6 Ft Surge Protector Power Strip - 8 Widely Outlets with 4 USB Ports, 3 Side Outlet Extender with 6 Feet Extension Cord, Flat Plug, Wall Mount, Desk USB Charging Station, ETL, White
products.verdict: Widely spaced outlets with a flat plug and wall mount.
products.description:
This strip lists 8 widely spaced outlets, 4 USB ports, a 6 ft cord, a flat plug, wall mounting and an ETL listing, for under $25. Wide spacing is the feature: big adapters and power bricks cover neighboring sockets on tight strips, wasting outlets.

It ranks last because no joule rating shows in our data, unlike every other strip here. That is the one number that measures protection, so its absence matters. The Nuetsa also has 8 outlets and a flat plug, but states 2700 joules. The wall mount is a bonus the others lack.

Buy it for a desk with chunky adapters and a wall to mount on. The caveat is simple: confirm the joule rating on the listing before ordering.
products.idealFor: Budget-conscious buyers who want widely spaced outlets to fit bulky adapters.
products.skipIf: You need a stated surge rating.

whatMatters.detail: Joules measure how much surge energy a strip can absorb over its life. Higher is better, and a very low number gives little margin. The picks here run from 790 to 4000 joules. Look for the number in the product title, and be wary of listings that call a strip surge protected without stating one, because that phrase alone proves nothing.

Bulky power bricks and adapters can block neighboring sockets on tightly spaced strips, wasting outlets. Widely spaced outlets avoid this. Check photos and the spacing description, because a 12-outlet strip may only give you eight usable plugs. The 8-outlet wide spacing model is designed for chunky adapters.

Built-in USB ports let you charge phones and tablets without a separate adapter, and they save outlets. The ALESTOR and Nuetsa each list four, the Yintar three. Check the USB count in the title and the charging wattage in the specs, since the Anker lists a 20W output and the others do not break it down.

Cord length decides how far the strip sits from the wall outlet. The Amazon Basics 12-outlet has 8 ft, and the others list 6 ft. Too short and you need an extension cord, which defeats the surge protection. Check the feet in the title, and measure the path from your outlet to the desk before you order.

An ETL listing means an independent lab certified the product to a safety standard. A protection LED shows when surge protection has worn out. The Amazon Basics 6-outlet has an LED indicator, and the ALESTOR, Nuetsa and Yintar list ETL. Look for both in the specs, and replace any strip that has no working indicator after a major surge.

faq.q: What do joules mean on a power strip?
faq.a: Joules show how much surge energy a strip can absorb. The picks here range from 790 to 4000 joules, and a higher number means more protection over the strip's life. Check it before outlet count.
Choosing by outlet count alone. A 12-outlet strip with a low joule rating protects less than a smaller strip with a high one. Check joules and the safety listing first, then count outlets.

faq.q: Is the ALESTOR worth it over the Amazon Basics 12-outlet?
faq.a: Only if you want 4 USB ports. The Amazon Basics 12-outlet offers 4000 joules against the ALESTOR's 2700 and an 8 ft cord, so it protects more for the same under $25. Choose the ALESTOR only for the USB ports.

faq.q: How do I fit big power bricks?
faq.a: Choose widely spaced outlets, like the wall-mount 8-outlet strip, or use a flat plug like the Nuetsa. Plug the largest adapters into the outer sockets to leave room for the rest, and keep the cord untangled.

faq.q: How do I know if protection still works?
faq.a: Some strips have an indicator light. The Amazon Basics 6-outlet has an LED protection indicator that shows whether the surge components still work. If the light goes out, replace the strip, since it has stopped protecting your gear.
The wide-spacing 8-outlet strip is listed as wall mountable. Check the others on the listing, and use a screw into a stud or a proper anchor so the weight of cords does not pull it down.

finalTake: Buy the Amazon Basics 12-outlet if surge headroom matters most and you have many plugs. Choose the ALESTOR for built-in USB charging, and the Nuetsa when the outlet is hidden behind the desk. Avoid relying on the 790 joule strip for expensive electronics, and replace any strip whose protection light goes out.
